newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela gov't approves new Orinoco oil partner.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela gov't approves new Orinoco oil partner.

text.p: Venezuela's Council of Ministers approved Friday the addition of Norway's Statoil and Norsk Hydro to a heavy oil joint-venture involving state oil subsidiary Maraven and Total, the government said in a press release.
The project, which was approved by Congress in 1993, originally included Japan's Itochu and Marubeni, but these companies pulled out last year.
Maraven said in August last year it was looking for a fifth partner in the scheme and named Elf Aqitaine and Phillips as possible takers.

The $5 billion project envisages 200,000 barrels per day of heavy crude production from the Zuata region of the Orinoco Oil Belt. It includes construction of a new deep conversion facility at Jose on the Caribbean coast which will export about 175,000 bpd of light sweet crude, due to come on stream in 2002.
